title: Kernel preemption jitter timeline sweep (Nsight)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for the Nsight timeline sweep investigating sudden tail-latency spikes correlated with kernel preemption and stream priority interactions. We saw intermittent 95/99th token latency regressions in production-like mixes when background maintenance kernels (prefetch, kv-cache warmers) run alongside decoder microbatches. Goal: reproduce with Nsight, isolate the preemption/jitter mechanism, and propose mitigations that preserve throughput and low median latency.

Summary of findings (short):
- Reproducible pattern: when a long-running maintenance kernel launches on a high-priority stream, in-flight decoder kernels on lower-priority streams show a burst of SM idle time followed by tightly packed kernel restarts -> large tail-latency spikes (P95 from ~45ms -> 180–240ms in our capture).
- Root cause hypothesis: hardware-level preemption + kernel serialization in the GPU runqueue creates wavefront tear-down and re-warm cycles (KV cache and persistent-kernel state must refill), leading to increased warp stall and decreased tensor-core utilization for several hundred microseconds per affected kernel.
- Secondary contributor: CUDA graph replay on decoder path exacerbates serialization because graph node boundaries align with the maintenance kernel launch windows, preventing overlap.

Environment and repro steps:
- HW: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (driver 530.41.03), CUDA 11.8 runtime.
- Build: serving-runtime main @ commit 7f3b2e (batcher + persistent-decoder + async-prefetch branches merged).
- Workload: 8 concurrent request threads generating 1–4 token microbatches; background maintenance job runs every 200ms to prefetch KV shards (large kernel ~80ms ideally runs at low priority).
- Nsight capture settings: system-wide timeline capture, kernel/warp metrics, SM__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active, warpstall_inst_executing.avg.pct, active_warps_per_sm, timeline resolution 1us, capture window 60s.
- Repro command snippets used: 
  - NVPROF/Nsight CLI: ncu --target-processes all --set full --metrics sm__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active,sm__warp_inst_executing.avg.pct -o profile.ncu \n  - Nsight Systems: nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --sample=1us -o nsight_timeline

Observed metrics & timeline notes:
- Before maintenance kernel: decoder kernels show high tensor-core utilization (~76% sustained), active_warps_per_sm ~24, warp_stall_mem_atomic and warp_stall_exec small. Median token kernel latency ~12–18ms.
- At maintenance kernel start: a 200–600us window of SM idle (active_warps_per_sm drops to ~6–8), then a cluster of decoder kernel restarts; during restarts tensor-core utilization drops to ~22–30%, warp_stall_inst_executing spikes, and occupancy (resident warps) is ~25% lower for 1–3 kernel launches.
- Tail latency mapping: the decoder kernel that was preempted suffers an extended completion time; in a typical mix we observed P95 token staging time jump from 45ms to ~220ms for 3–7% of requests in sample capture.
- CUDA graph interaction: decoder uses CUDA graphs to reduce kernel launch overhead. When the maintenance kernel launches mid-replay, graph replay gets serialized behind the maintenance kernel (graph replay does not preempt; it is queued), increasing serialization windows.

Hypotheses considered (and how we tried to invalidate them):
1) Driver bugs / known firmware race: checked against two driver versions (525.x and 530.x) — behavior consistent across both, so not specific to single driver build.
2) Host-side stalls: instrumented CPU threads for blocking syscalls; no synchronous host waits mapped to the idle windows.
3) PCIe interference: captures show the sm idle windows align to kernel lifecycle events on the GPU, not DMA floods.
4) Kernel resource starvation due to occupancy regression: observed minor occupancy drop but the large factor is teardown/wakeup rewarm overhead, not only occupancy.

Quick trace excerpt (simplified):
- T=12.134s: decoder-kernel-A (low-prio stream) running
- T=12.136s: maintenance-kernel-B (high-prio stream) launches -> persistent kernel preemption occurs
- T=12.1365s: decoder-kernel-A tears down; SMs go idle ~250us
- T=12.1368s: decoder-kernel-A resumes/relaunched, but warp occupancy and tensor-core utilization ramp slowly over ~600us
- Net effect: decoder-kernel-A wall-clock increased by ~0.8–1.1ms in this microtrace; repeated across multiple microbatches accumulates to observed P95 spike.

Why this matters for serving-runtime:
- Even sub-millisecond repeated penalties stack across token generation loops (30–60 tokens) and across request queues, producing perceivable P95/P99 regressions for customers.
- The current default policy of putting maintenance kernels on high-priority streams (to ensure they complete quickly) is counterproductive for latency-sensitive decoding.

Potential mitigations (ranked):
1) Policy change: run maintenance kernels at an adaptive lower priority and schedule them only during detected low-inflight-windows. Simple to implement in the runtime scheduler. (Low-risk, high-impact initial change).
2) Co-operative yields: refactor maintenance kernels to be interruptible at safe points (split into smaller tiles that yield) so they don't trigger long preemption cycles. Requires kernel code changes and validation.
3) CUDA-graph-aware scheduling: ensure graph replay is pinned to priority streams or serialized in a way that avoids being starved/serialized by background jobs. Consider moving graph replay to a dedicated high-bandwidth stream but with throttled admission, or convert critical decode paths to inline launches for fine-grained preemption control.
4) Stream-priority tuning + preemption smoothing: stagger maintenance kernel launches in time and use different priorities to avoid synchronous preemption of many SMs. Could be combined with jittered scheduling windows.
5) Driver/OpenHW escalation: open a ticket with NVIDIA if cooperative split/preemption smoothing is insufficient; there may be HW preemption effects we cannot fully mitigate in software.

Immediate experiments to implement (next short-term tasks):
- Implement adaptive priority policy in a feature branch: "adaptive-maintenance-priority". Gate by in-flight microbatch count and request latency. (Owner: Liam).
- Prototype tile-splitting for prefetch kernel (split 80ms job into 8x10ms tiles) and re-run Nsight capture to verify rewarm profile. (Owner: Ravi).
- Create a synthetic stress harness that replays production arrival patterns (bursty token generation + periodic maintenance) to test at scale. (Owner: Samira).
- Add finer-grained telemetry: per-kernel preemption events and preemption-duration histograms in the console so we can correlate with customer P95. (Owner: Observability team ticket O11).

Longer-term ideas:
- Consider a lightweight admission controller in the serving runtime that models cost of preemption (estimated resume cost) and trades off short-term maintenance progress for reduced tail-latency risk.
- Explore alternative hardware-level modes (if available) like cooperative groups or stream-ordered memory region hints to reduce rewarm cost.

Open questions and TODOs:
- How often does this happen in our different instance families (A100 vs H100)? We only tested A100; schedule H100 captures.
- Are certain model sizes (bigger KV size) more prone to larger rewarm cost? Need to sweep model context sizes.
- Does pinned vs pageable host memory allocation for KV buffers change preemption penalty? Quick check indicated marginal impact, but run dedicated test.

Files/attachments referenced in this doc:
- nsight_captures/preempt_timeline_oct04.nsys (large, on GDrive root)
- traces/cluster_synthetic_2025-10-02.csv (request arrival times used by harness)
- plots/preemption_cdf_oct04.png (P95/P99 comparison)

Action items (owners):
- Liam: land adaptive-priority prototype and run basic perf regression suite (due 2025-10-20).
- Ravi: produce prefetch tile-split branch and run Nsight capture (due 2025-10-22).
- Samira: extend synthetic harness to hit larger scale and upload traces (due 2025-10-18).
- Observability: add preemption-duration histogram (create ticket O11-2, due 2025-11-01).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an early-stage working doc — captures are large (1–2GB). If you want raw capture files or help reproducing, ping me in #eng-serving-runtime or DM.
- Priority for shipping: quick policy change (adaptive priority) first, kernel splitting second. If reviewers disagree on approach, let's discuss tradeoffs in next sync.

Preliminary verdict: kernel preemption-induced rewarm cycles are a real, measurable contributor to tail-latency spikes in our decoding workloads. Software scheduling mitigations appear promising and relatively low-risk; hardware/driver escalation is last resort.

-- Samira
